incident-report#description: A batch of confirmed security incidents. Source: the organization's SOAR / case-management system. The envelope carries the organization identity once; incidents live in the incidents[] array. Elements do NOT contain org_id/sender_id. tlp is per element — incidents are independent and differ in sensitivity.
incident-report#/properties/org_id: The organization where the incidents occurred (data owner). The sender is NOT here — it is identified via the x-org-id header and the HMAC signature. One organization per request.
incident-report#/properties/collected_at: OPTIONAL diagnostic field: when the batch was assembled by the integration. collected_at − updated_at = delivery lag. If omitted, the server's receive time is used (less precise: it also includes network and queue latency).
incident-report#/properties/incidents/it: UUID v5 per guide §1.5 formula: uuidv5(17e9f2a9-2473-5a70-b622-f121ae871cb0, org_id + '|' + source_case_id). NEVER generated randomly.
The organization's own case number. report_id is derived from it, so it is required and must not change during the incident's life.
Case system name: TheHive, XSOAR, Sentinel, Splunk SOAR, QRadar SOAR, Updive.
report_ids of OTHER incidents the analyst considers related (duplicate, stages of one campaign, etc.). NOT needed to send an update. Must NOT contain its own report_id — the backend checks this.
Sensitivity level of this incident. Not in the envelope but per incident — incidents are independent and differ in sensitivity.
finding_info.uid values of the related alerts. Located directly in the incidents[] element, at the same level as lifecycle/technical. CVE linkage happens through this.

OCSF Incident Finding status: 1 New, 2 In Progress, 3 On Hold, 4 Resolved, 5 Closed. 0 (Unknown) and 99 (Other) are DELIBERATELY absent — a case is always in one of these five. Mapping from source systems: Appendix B.10.
When the organization's tooling FIRST detected the activity (not when the case was opened). Starting point of every time_to_* calculation.
When the case was opened in the SOAR. opened_at − detected_at = triage lag.
When this particular version of the report was produced.
Required when status_id = 5 (Closed).
MTTA: seconds from detected_at to the first analyst action. Based on SOAR data.
MTTC: seconds from detected_at to containment. Based on SOAR data.
MTTR: seconds from detected_at to full resolution. Based on SOAR data.

Post-investigation verdict: 0 Unknown, 1 False Positive, 2 True Positive, 3 Disregard, 4 Suspicious, 5 Benign, 6 Test, 7 Insufficient Data, 8 Security Risk, 9 Managed Externally, 10 Duplicate. 99 (Other) is DELIBERATELY absent. Mapping: Appendix B.11.
ENISA RSIT 1.3 first level.
ENISA RSIT 1.3 second level. MUST match the chosen event_category. Optional: no SOAR has RSIT natively; leaving it empty is better than a wrong value.
Sanitized summary. NO raw logs, IPs, logins or command lines.
OCSF: 0 Unknown, 1 Informational, 2 Low, 3 Medium, 4 High, 5 Critical, 99 Other. Same scale as alert telemetry.
MITRE ATT&CK, three levels: tactic → techniques → sub-techniques. Tactic is REQUIRED (it cannot be derived from the technique: one technique may belong to several tactics). Each tactic appears once.
Technique ID. Sub-techniques do NOT go here — they go into sub_techniques[].
A sub-technique is never sent without its parent: if the source only gives T1110.001, the connector derives T1110 from the ID and writes it as the parent technique.

asset_uid values of the affected assets. Filled in once the assets are known. If no internal asset was involved or the scope is not yet determined, send [] and fill it in on the next lifecycle update. Links to asset_inventory.assets[].asset_uid. Write the asset's hostname, not the SOAR's internal asset ID. Normalization: no whitespace, lowercase, FQDN truncated at the first dot (WEB01.corp.local → web01); no IP addresses (guide §2.4.7).
IOCs. An empty array only when the source system has no observables. Normalization is mandatory (§2.3): refang, lowercase, RFC 1918 filtered out.
Actions performed within the case, free text. NO hostnames, IPs, logins or employee names.
NIST SP 800-61 response phase. Differs from status_id (workflow state).
Free-text note at case closure. The closure REASON is not here — it is in verdict_id. NO confidential data.
Case chronology, FULL history. Re-sent in full on every update. Comment TEXT is not sent — only the fact that a comment was added, and its time. No size limit.
Required when type = status_changed.
Required when type = severity_changed.
alert#description: Request body — an ARRAY of alerts. The envelope carries the organization identity once; alerts live in the alerts[] array. Elements do NOT contain org_id or collected_at — those are in the envelope. additionalProperties:false — fields not in the schema are rejected.
alert#/properties/org_id: The organization the alerts belong to (data owner). The sender is NOT here. One organization per request.
alert#/properties/collected_at: When the batch was collected by the integration (ISO 8601 UTC). Unlike 'time' inside an alert — that one is epoch ms.
alert#/properties/alerts/items/propertie: Always 1 (Create). An alert is immutable; the lifecycle lives in incident telemetry.
When the observed activity ended (epoch ms). Paired with start_time: if end_time is present, start_time is required and start_time <= end_time must hold.
0 Unknown, 1 Informational, 2 Low, 3 Medium, 4 High, 5 Critical, 99 Other. 0 is used honestly when the source gives no severity.
tenant_uid is DELIBERATELY absent — attribution is via org_id.
The source tool's own ID. Stable. Idempotency key and the link point to incident.technical.alerts[].
Rule name. NO event text or values.
hostname — the key linking to asset_inventory.assets[].asset_uid (short, lowercase name).
MAC address, lowercase. Matched against technical.mac_addresses[] on the asset.
0 Unknown, 1 Hostname, 2 IP, 3 MAC, 4 User Name, 5 Email, 6 URL, 7 File Name, 8 Hash, 10 Resource UID, 11 Port, 18 CVE uid, 99 Other. 13/15/19 are not sent for privacy reasons.
Alert triage state: 0 Unknown, 1 New, 2 In Progress, 3 Suppressed, 4 Resolved, 5 Archived, 99 Other. DIFFERS from incident status_id.
asset-inventory#description: Organization assets. A common core plus one class-specific object. Fields of the registry classes (information, process, personnel, site, organization) are defined per ISO/IEC 27002:2022 and 27005:2022. The backend works on an UPSERT basis: an asset that is not sent is not deleted, its last_seen simply is not refreshed. TLP:RED.
asset-inventory#/properties/assets/items: Stable unique ID. Does not change between snapshots. In the personnel class, NO name/login/email — an anonymous ID only.
MUST match asset_class (Appendix F).
The ONLY way to remove an asset: decommissioned. Absence from the list is not removal.
The staleness rule applies only to assets with provenance=discovered.
asset_uids of related assets (application → server, data → database, process → application, responsible person → assets).
Common object for the hardware / software / network / service / information_resource / security_tool classes. REQUIRED in these six classes, FORBIDDEN in the others.
Full hostname / FQDN.
OCSF os.type_id (same as in alerts): 0 Unknown, 100 Windows, 101 Windows Mobile, 200 Linux, 201 Android, 300 macOS, 301 iOS, 302 iPadOS, 400 Solaris, 401 AIX, 402 HP-UX, 99 Other.
MAC addresses, lowercase. Fallback key for linking with device.mac in alerts.
Protection class of the automated system against unauthorized access (O'z DSt 2814:2014; O'zMSt 816:2025 §7.9.4). Only for the information_system and industrial_control_system types.
Internet exposure. May differ from IP scope (NAT/reverse proxy).
Only what the organization knows. NSOC fills in CVSS and KEV itself from the CVE ID.

Object for the information class. Optional; an empty object {} is valid. Basis: O'zMSt 816:2025 (Annex L — access restriction, integrity and availability categories); ISO/IEC 27002:2022 5.33, 5.34, 8.10–8.13, 8.24.

Access restriction categories (O'zMSt 816:2025, Annex L): SS — top secret, S — secret (state secrets); DSP — for official use, KT — trade secret, BT — banking secret, PD — personal data, KO — organization-confidential; OD — public data. Several may be combined; OD only alone.
Integrity category (O'zMSt 816:2025, Annex L): V — high, N — low, '-' — no requirement.
Availability category (O'zMSt 816:2025, Annex L): B — uninterrupted (outage <= 1 minute), V — high (<= 1 hour), S — medium (<= 12 hours), N — low (> 12 hours).
Data categories. Several may be selected.
Whether personal data is present (ISO 27002 5.34).
Band of the number of PII subjects. NO exact number — a band only.
Storage location — data residency (ISO 27002 5.23).
Retention period in days (ISO 27002 5.33, 8.10). 0 — no period defined.
Cryptographic protection status (ISO 27002 8.24).
Whether masking/pseudonymization is applied (ISO 27002 8.11).
Whether a data leakage prevention tool covers it (ISO 27002 8.12).
Backup status (ISO 27002 8.13).
Which regulatory requirements apply (ISO 27002 5.31, 5.34).
Object for the process class. Optional; an empty object {} is valid. Basis: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 5.29, 5.30, 5.2; ISO/IEC 27005:2022 7.3.2.
asset_uid of the process owner — an anonymous ID in the personnel class (ISO 27002 5.2). NO names.
Whether a disruption of the process directly affects citizens. Sets national priority.
Availability category (O'zMSt 816:2025, Annex L): B — outage <= 1 minute, V — <= 1 hour, S — <= 12 hours, N — > 12 hours.
Business impact analysis results (ISO 27002 5.30 — BIA).
Recovery Time Objective — target recovery time, in minutes.
Recovery Point Objective — tolerable data-loss window, in minutes.
Maximum Tolerable Period of Disruption — the longest outage that can be endured.
Continuity plan status (ISO 27002 5.29, 5.30).
Whether the process can be run manually when IT is down.
Overall consequence of a disruption (ISO 27005 7.3.2).

Object for the personnel class. Optional; an empty object {} is valid. PERSONAL DATA IS FORBIDDEN — no name, login, email, phone, job-title text or date of birth. Basis: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 5.2, 5.3, 6.1–6.7, 8.2.
Whether the record represents a single person, a role or a group. Recommended: role or group — anonymity is stronger.
Number of people in the role/group when represents=role or group.
Role category (ISO 27002 5.2). NOT a free-text job title.
Employment type (ISO 27002 6.2, 5.19).
Whether privileged access is held (ISO 27002 8.2).
Areas of privileged access (ISO 27002 8.2). Only when privileged_access=true.
Whether a segregation-of-duties violation has been identified (ISO 27002 5.3).
Whether pre-employment screening was done (ISO 27002 6.1).
Whether a confidentiality agreement is signed (ISO 27002 6.6).
Awareness and training status (ISO 27002 6.3).
Whether remote work access is granted (ISO 27002 6.7).
Information categories the person/role has access to (O'zMSt 816:2025, Annex L codes).
Object for the site class. Optional; an empty object {} is valid. NO EXACT ADDRESS — region code only. Basis: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 7.1–7.5, 7.11, 7.12.
Facility type.
ISO 3166-2:UZ region code. NO street address, building number or coordinates. FOREIGN — outside Uzbekistan.
Form of ownership (ISO 27002 5.19 — supplier responsibility for external premises).
Whether designated as a secure area (ISO 27002 7.1, 7.3, 7.6).
Physical access control measures (ISO 27002 7.2).
Physical monitoring measures (ISO 27002 7.4).
Supporting utilities (ISO 27002 7.11).
Known natural and environmental threats (ISO 27002 7.5).
Whether crown_jewel or high-criticality assets are located at this site.
Object for the organization class. Optional; an empty object {} is valid. Basis: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 5.19–5.23; ISO/IEC 27005:2022 7.2.
The organization's role in the context of this asset (ISO 27002 5.19, 5.21, 5.23).
LEGAL ENTITY registry code (STIR/INN). NO codes of natural persons or sole proprietors. Used to detect supply-chain overlap at the national level.
ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 jurisdiction code (ISO 27002 5.21 — ICT supply chain).
Types of access granted to the organization (ISO 27002 5.19, 5.20).
Contract coverage (ISO 27002 5.20).
Whether the contract includes an incident-notification obligation.
Verified certifications (ISO 27002 5.21, 5.22).
Date of the last security review (ISO 27002 5.22).
Whether there is a dependency on this supplier with no alternative (ISO 27005 7.2 — concentration risk).
Object for the intangible class. Fields not yet defined — an empty object {} for now.
